title: Skid-Steer Kerf-and-Ladder Lunar Digger with Screw-Tilt Pour
problem_restatement: Build a blind-operated lunar digger that traverses, loosens, collects, contains and discharges BP-1 soil within 60 kg mass and 1.0 by 0.5 by 0.5 m stowed box.
mechanism_sentence: Four grouser wheels drive a 46 kg machine that cuts a 100 mm wide slot 50 mm deep, buckets lift the loose soil into a half-full 20 L hopper, and a screw meters the 15 kg load out as the hopper tilts to clear the bin lip by 0.15 m.
decisive_choices: Chose four-wheel skid-steer with rigid grouser wheels C9 over tank tracks C8 because traction 294 N versus cut 32.9 N with 15.6 kPa pressure avoids clog and slip with same soil.
Chose narrow-kerf trenching chain C36 over full-width ladder C1 and scraper C3 and milling drum C31 because 11 N kerf draft versus 32.9 N full width fits same 294 N traction and 16.4 W power.

Chose auger live-bottom with rear tilt C37 over plain tilting hopper plus vibrator C5 because metered pour with same 0.55 m pivot clearing 0.40 m lip by 0.15 m holds blind accuracy with tip factor 1.69.
open_question: Will cohesive BP-1 arch over the 150 mm outlet and what screw torque breaks it for reliable discharge?
transfer_line: Load: narrow kerf chain -> bucket ladder -> steep wedge hopper | Measured: dig camera -> sealed station operator

assumed_constraints.constraint: Working stress capped near 15 ksi for 6061-T6 aluminium tube frame
BP-1 friction 39 to 51 deg needs steep smooth hopper walls for flow

concept.working_principle: Narrow 100 mm kerf chain cuts 50 mm deep slot at 11 N draft well below 294 N traction, wide bucket ladder lifts side spoil in 112 s to 15 kg half-full 20 L steep wedge hopper, rear tilt plus live-bottom screw meters pour over 0.40 m bin lip with 0.15 m clearance guided by cameras plus fiducial with heartbeat stop and odometry reset.

parts.name: folding wheel arms
parts.function: stows in box then widens track

parts.name: drive and dig and mast cameras

constraint_table.how_shown: Mass sum calc shows 46 kg versus 60 kg limit with 14 kg margin.

constraint_table.constraint: Stowed envelope within 1.0 by 0.5 by 0.5 m box
constraint_table.how_shown: Envelope simulation shows stowed size fits inside start box with deployed track widening.

measurement_chain.name: forward drive plus dig plus mast cameras
measurement_chain.interface: optical view of buckets and bin fiducial

measurement_chain.name: onboard video encoder and current limit

fabrication_steps.description: Weld the twin-tube aluminium chassis first, because wheels, ladder and hopper all bolt to it
fabrication_steps.method: TIG-welded 6061-T6 tube, 25.4 mm outside 3 mm wall

fabrication_steps.description: Bolt folding arms and grouser wheels to chassis, because track width and spin gap set stability
fabrication_steps.method: Bolted aluminium arms, 200 mm diameter wheels with 10 mm grousers

fabrication_steps.description: Mount narrow kerf chain and bucket ladder to front mounts, because chain clearance and chute gap set dig path
fabrication_steps.method: Bolted steel chain and ladder, 100 mm kerf width 50 mm depth

fabrication_steps.description: Mount steep wedge hopper on rear pivots with live-bottom screw, because tilt pour clears bin lip
fabrication_steps.method: Steel wedge hopper, 20 L volume 60 deg walls 150 mm outlet

fabrication_steps.description: Wire battery packs and cameras to fused bus and computer last, because power and views prove before blind run
fabrication_steps.method: Fused 24 V 20 Ah LiFePO4 bus, drive and dig cameras

risks.risk: BP-1 arches over outlet and pour stalls
risks.mitigation: Run half-full 15 kg trips and bench-test arching plus screw torque after build

risks.risk: Rear tilt tips machine or misses bin blind
risks.mitigation: Keep level-ground pour, fiducial creep align and heartbeat stop with 0.308 m stop

novelty_claim: Narrow kerf loosening feeding wide ladder pickup with screw-metered tilt pour under camera-only blind operation

figure_spec.system_view: side view of ladder feeding wedge hopper with rear tilt over bin plus top view of deployed track

open_questions: Will cohesive BP-1 arch over the 150 mm outlet and what screw torque breaks it?
How fast does the cutting edge wear in BP-1 before draft rises beyond margin?
Can the mast camera see the bin fiducial clearly enough for final align in dust?
